title: Uptime ownership radar — 60d cross-functional activation
content:
Purpose:
Create a lightweight, practical 60-day activation plan ("radar") for establishing service-level ownership across product, platform, and SRE teams. The goal is to move from vague SLAs and ad-hoc runbooks to concrete SLOs, mapped owners, and a small set of experiments that prove the operational model for model-serving workloads.

Context / why now:
- Rapid growth in hosted/dedicated traffic has exposed gaps in ownership at service boundaries (model variants, routing, cache invalidation).
- Product launches planned in Q2 require predictable latency and availability for low-latency endpoints.
- We need a repeatable onboarding pattern for feature teams to adopt SLOs and error-budget discipline without heavy ops overhead.

Scope (what this radar covers):
- Core: 3 pilot services (text-generation-hosted, embeddings-batch, reranking-api).
- Activities: SLO definition, owner assignments, dashboards, runbook fragments, canary rollout recipe, and two signal experiments (latency-pressure and cache-thrash).
- Excluded: full org-wide SLO rollout (this is a pilot; lessons will feed broader program).

Desired outcomes (60d):
- Each pilot has a documented SLO (latency & availability) and a named owner (primary + backup).
- Dashboards streaming telemetry including p50/p95/p99, request volume, error-rate, and error-budget burn.
- One automated canary gate + rollback policy wired into CI for feature deploys.
- Two documented experiments completed with notes and recommended tweaks to serving runtime (batching/kv-cache adjustments).

Success metrics:
- 3/3 pilots: SLO docs + owner + live dashboard (pass = 3).
- Canary gate prevents at least one unsafe rollout during the pilot window (observable in deployment logs).
- Error-budget alerts triggered and routed to owners with <15 minute handoff time during experiments.
- Collect qualitative feedback from product + platform teams; target NPS-like score >= 6/10 on ease of adoption.

Roles & responsibilities (working proposals):
- SRE lead (Aisha Patel): project convener, telemetry template, runbook skeleton.
- Platform engineer (Liam O'Connor): CI canary gate, rollout automation, infra quotas for pilots.
- Product partner (Priya Menon): define user-impact thresholds, prioritize pilot services and traffic shaping for experiments.
- Applied ML eng (Diego Alvarez): provide model-variant behavior matrix and expected latency distributions.
- Observability engineer (Rina Chen): dashboard templates, alert routing, synthetic load hooks.
- Exec sponsor (Elena Novak): stakeholder escalations and prioritization nudges.

Week-by-week 60-day plan (high level):
- Week 0 (kickoff): align on pilots, confirm owners, runbook template, create Jira epic SRE-4721, schedule twice-weekly syncs.
- Week 1: draft SLOs for each pilot (availability + latency buckets), baseline telemetry ingestion.
- Week 2: instrument dashboards; smoke tests for metrics correctness; define error-budget burn policy.
- Week 3: implement canary gate in CI for one pilot; create rollback recipe and Slack alert channel.
- Week 4: run first controlled traffic experiment (latency-pressure) on pilot #1; capture burn, validate alerts.
- Week 5: iterate on batching/kv-cache parameters based on experiment; update recommendations in Optimize backlog.
- Week 6: propagate canary gate to pilot #2 and pilot #3; run second experiment (cache-thrash) on pilot #2.
- Week 7: finalize runbook fragments; rehearse an on-call drill with owners; capture time-to-handoff metrics.
- Week 8: retro, NPS-style feedback, handoff doc to reliability program for scaling, write lessons-learned doc.

Kickoff checklist (quick):
- [ ] Confirm pilot service owners and backups.
- [ ] Create monitoring dashboards (template link in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Wire basic alerts to owner rotation (PagerDuty/Slack).
- [ ] Add canary gate ticket to infra backlog.
- [ ] Schedule first two-week experiment window.

Experiment design quick notes (two pilots):
1) Latency-pressure experiment:
   - Traffic: increase tail-latency inducing requests via synthetic load to mimic longer prompts and rare model paths.
   - Observables: p99 latency, queues, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate.
   - Success: system remains within error-budget or canary gate blocks rollout.
2) Cache-thrash experiment:
   - Traffic: many unique prefixes to reduce cache hits, measure effect on token latency and cost per request.
   - Observables: cache hit rate, p95 latency, token cost delta.
   - Success: identify a small set of mitigations (prefix caching TTL, batching policy adjust) that recover p95 within SLO.

Communication cadence & rituals:
- Twice-weekly 30m syncs (Mon/Wed) during active weeks; weekly check-in after Week 4.
- Shared workspace: #sre-uptime-radar (linked in linked_artifacts), Confluence canvas for artifacts.
- Weekly digest: short email to exec sponsor with 3 bullets (progress, blockers, requests).

Risks & mitigations (raw):
- Risk: Too many owners > diffused accountability. Mitigation: require primary + single backup; owners must sign acceptance note in Jira.
- Risk: Observability gaps (missing telemetry). Mitigation: declare critical metric list; no pilot advances without those metrics.
- Risk: Experiment collateral damage to customers. Mitigation: traffic shaping, synthetic tenants, strict canary limits, immediate rollback policy.

Open questions (notes to self):
- Do we treat model variant fallbacks as separate SLOs or as a dimension of the same SLO? Proposal: single user-facing SLO with an annotated mapping to internal model-variant profiles.
- Who owns cost anomalies surfaced during experiments? Platform or product? Need explicit decision.
- Should error-budget routing go to product first or SRE first? Current lean: route to owner (product) with SRE cc for first 30d.

Artifacts to deliver at close of 60d:
- SLO docs for each pilot (short readme style).
- Dashboard + alert templates (shareable dashboards).
- Canary gate recipe + CI plugin example.
- Experiment journal (what we ran, data, decisions).
- Adoption playbook (steps for next 10 services).

Next immediate actions (today):
- Create Jira epic SRE-4721 and assign sub-tasks to owners (Aisha to create, owners to accept).
- Standup short Slack poll to pick experiment windows (Priya).
- Platform: provision canary quota for pilot services (Liam).

Notes / informal: this document is intentionally lightweight. Keep friction low for teams to adopt — prioritize one clear owner per service, one observable dashboard, and one automated gate. Capture all learning in the experiment journal so the full reliability program can convert this radar into a repeatable onboarding kit.

Version history:
